flashcard_questions.q: Why does the pilot himself have no voice in the poem?
flashcard_questions.a: His silence mirrors the way his family silenced him after his return.

flashcard_questions.q: Which weapon does the pilot carry in the cockpit?
What does the word ‘incantations’ suggest about the pilot?
flashcard_questions.a: Patriotic propaganda has worked on him almost like a spell.

flashcard_questions.q: Which simile compares the fishing boats to something celebratory?
Which national symbol do the shoals of fish resemble from the air?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘A huge flag waved first one way then the other.’

flashcard_questions.q: How does the pilot’s wife treat him after his return?
flashcard_questions.a: She never speaks again in his presence and will not meet his eyes.

flashcard_questions.q: Which verb shows the children were taught to reject their father?
Which question closes the poem Kamikaze?
flashcard_questions.a: Which had been the better way to die.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the feminine French form of the title tell us?
flashcard_questions.a: The speaker of The Emigrée is female.

flashcard_questions.q: Which violent verb shows the sunlight memory is burned into the speaker?
Which metaphor makes time an invading military force?
Which simile shows the remembered city as fragile and controllable?
Which final image proves that the light still exists for the speaker?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘My shadow falls as evidence of sunlight.’

flashcard_questions.q: What does the hostile ‘they’ reveal about the speaker’s new home?
flashcard_questions.a: She is treated as an outsider, facing racism or xenophobia.

notes: 15 cards across both poems, 9 on Kamikaze and 6 on The Emigrée: 6 quotation-recall fronts, 5 quotation-to-effect (‘incantations’, ‘learned’, ‘branded’, the flag, the wife’s silence), 2 form-and-voice cards (the daughter as narrator, the silenced pilot), 1 title card (the feminine French form), 1 theme-to-evidence (the hostile ‘they’). ‘Simile’, ‘sibilance’, ‘personification’, ‘narrative voice’ and the two poet-biography terms dropped as glossary restatements; the sibilance line was cut because the honest card duplicates the simile card’s effect. All quotations verbatim from the lesson content.
